name: Legendary Mesmerist
body:
The Astral Plane is the realm of ideas, the summation of all thought and emotion. A place to which all beings with a mind and a will, by their nature, are connected. A mesmerist, then, is a magic user who awoke to this connection. When they look upon themselves, and others, they also glimpse the true self in that silver expanse, to be improved, shattered or molded as those who dare see fit.

Role: Unlike its counterpart, the legendary mesmerist commits to magic as a full caster. Their direct combat ability is minimal. However, they excel in debilitating opponents, exploiting weaknesses or creating new ones, and converting others to the cause. In manipulation, and finding secrets, be they plucked from the cosmos or from someone’s h e a d , the legendary mesmerist is second to none.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d8.

Starting Wealth: 3d6 x 10 gp (average 105 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The legendary mesmerist’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (all) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), Spellcraft (Int), Stealth (Dex), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Points at each Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Class Features
Weapon and Armor Proficiency

A legendary mesmerist is proficient with all simple weapons, plus the cat o’ nine tails, hand crossbow, sap, sword cane, and whip. They are proficient with light armor, but not with shields.

Spellcasting

A legendary mesmerist casts psychic spells drawn from the legendary mesmerist spell list. This includes all spells from the classic mesmerist’s spell list, with additions and changes listed in this book(see below). They can cast any spell they know without preparing it ahead of time. To learn or cast a spell, a legendary mesmerist must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell’s level. The saving throw DC against a spell is 10 + the spell’s level + the legendary mesmerist’s Charisma modifier. R legendary mesmerist can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on Table: The Legendary Mesmerist. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high Charisma score. The legendary mesmerist’s selection of spells is limited. R mesmerist begins play knowing four 0-level spells, two 1st-level spells of the mesmerist’s choice, one of which must be a focus spell, and one bonus spell determined by their hypnotic focus (See page 5). At each new mesmerist level, they learn one or more new spells. Whenever a mesmerist gains access to a new spell level, the first spell they learn must be a focus spell, as indicated on Table: Legendary Mesmerist Spells Known. Unlike a mesmerist’s spells per day, the number of spells a mesmerist knows isn’t affected by his Charisma score; the numbers on the table are fixed. It 4th level and every even numbered level thereafter, a mesmerist can choose to learn a new spell in place of one they already know. In effect, the mesmerist loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and it must be at least 1 level lower than the highest-level mesmerist spell the mesmerist can cast. A mesmerist can swap only a single spell at any given level. Focus spells, whether they’re swapped out through these means or otherwise, must be replaced with other focus spells. R mesmerist need not prepare spells in advance. They can cast any mesmerist spell they know at any time, assuming they have not yet used up their allotment of spells per day for the spell’s level.

Focus Casting

At 1st level, the legendary mesmerist gains two additional spell slots, called their focus slots. The focus slots are always the level of the highest-level spell slot available to the mesmerist. They may only be used to cast focus spells. R mesmerist’s available focus spells are determined by their hypnotic focus (see below), including a single bonus spell they learn at 1st level. They also add spells listed for their focus not yet on the mesmerist spell list to their spell list.

The mesmerist may apply metamagic feats to a focus spell without increasing its casting time. A mesmerist can learn spells on their focus’ list even if it would be normally limited to a given race, without instruction from a member of that race.

Hypnotic Focus (Su)

A mesmerist can, with some effort, focus their mind upon a creature within 30 feet, +5 feet every even level. Initiating and maintaining the hypnotic focus demands effort on the mesmerist’s part. How this effort manifests depends on the focus. Hypnotic foci may have the capacity to target more than one creature at a time. When they do, they impose a -1 penalty to Will saving throws. Any foci targeting a single creature imposes a -2 penalty instead, whether or not it is capable of targeting more than one. Choose a focus at character creation. Once made, the choice cannot be changed. A mesmerist can double the penalties of their hypnotic focus by meeting its listed criteria, grants a bonus spell, and a bonus feat, for which the mesmerist need not meet the prerequisites. Penalties imposed by the hypnotic focus are mind-affecting, but the hypnotic focus itself is not. The mesmerist is automatically aware whenever the penalties do not apply to a target. R mesmerist’s focus remains in effect on a target for as long as the mesmerist is alive and conscious, until the target dies, the distance between the mesmerist and a target exceeds its range. The target has no awareness or memory of being the target of a mesmerist’s focus, unless the mesmerist wants it to. All hypnotic foci require, at the least, awareness the target is within range. Unless otherwise stated, the mesmerist applies hypnotic focus to a single target at a time, as a swift action. Ending hypnotic focus on any number of targets is always a nonaction. Mind blank doesn’t prevent the mesmerist from using their hypnotic focus on a target. The penalties from multiple mesmerists’ foci do not stack, nor do they stack with penalties from evil eye hexes or hypnotic stare. The mesmerist’s will is not to be denied – By expending a spell slot, the mesmerist can use a mind-affecting spell-like ability from the universal school, unique to each focus, on targets of their hypnotic focus as a full-round action. These abilities are collectively called will enforcement. The effect of a will enforcement is broken down into two parts:

Will: The changes in the target’s mind that benefit the mesmerist. The target may attempt a Will saving throw to resist this effect. The DC is the same as that of the expended spell slot.
Enforcement: The penalty the target suffers for noncompliance, enforcement subtly breaks a small but crucial part of the target’s mind, rendering it more vulnerable. This is instantaneous, and not subject to the saving throw or spell resistance. The enforcement can be suppressed any time by bowing to the mesmerist’s will, acting as though the saving throw failed. This need not be voluntary. The target may oppose the mesmerist’s will again as a free action, but at the cost of the enforcement effect returning as part of that action. Unless otherwise stated, will enforcement’s initial numerical effects equal the penalty of the mesmerist’s hypnotic focus suffered by the target at the time of use, or the level of the expended spell slot, whichever is lower. Effects tied to this initial number are lessened by rest as though they were ability damage. Once they are reduced to 0, will enforcement ends. The penalties of will enforcement stack with bold foci, but not with itself. Lesser restoration returns the target to normal. The mesmerist can use will enforcement a number of times per day equal to their level.
Bold Focus

As the mesmerist becomes more comfortable prying minds open and pulling at heartstrings, they can use their hypnotic focus to apply a wider variety of effects on its targets. This is identical to the classic mesmerist’s bold stare class feature. In addition to bold foci available in this book, any bold stare available to the classic mesmerist may be taken as a bold focus, with the exception of psychic inception.

Lessen: The target is treated as if it had 1 fewer Hit Die for the purposes of spells and abilities.
Mindgrip: The DC of checks made to identify or dispel the mesmerist’s spells on the target is increased by an amount equal to the penalty.
Phobiac: Whenever you apply this bold focus, choose a damage type. Whenever the target is subject to that damage type, it takes untyped nonlethal damage equal to the penalty. The damage is dealt even if the target has resistance or immunity to the original damage type. This is a fear and pain effect.
Thoughtfade: Whenever the target of the focus casts a spell that requires concentration or a thought component, it must pass a concentration check(DC = 10 + the mesmerist’s level + focus penalty). Creatures with the mental static ability are immune to this effect.
Tremors: The penalty also applies to Disable Device, Escape Artist and Sleight of Hand checks, as well as concentration checks made to cast or maintain spells with somatic components.
Voicecrack: Spells with vocal components cast by the target suffer a 10% spell failure chance. While the focus penalty is doubled, the chance increases to 15%.
Ensure: The hypnotic focus suppresses its target’s morale bonuses by an amount equal to its penalty, to a minimum of 0.
Impose Psyche (Su)

A legendary mesmerist’s magic intuits the presence of minds around them, imposing their will and twisting ideas where others would find no grip. This demands a great deal of finagling and mental acrobatics from the mesmerist, who may only impose on psyches a number of times per day equal to 3 + their Charisma modifier. Imposing a psyche requires a different set of actions depending on the target. All such actions require the mesmerist’s hypnotic focus to be set on their target, and, unless otherwise stated, last as long as the mesmerist maintains focus on the target. The mesmerist must pass a Knowledge check to recall how the creature’s defenses function each time impose psyche is used. The mesmerist must personally grasp the underpinnings of the target’s immunities; an ally’s check result cannot be used as a substitute. It 1st level, the mesmerist gains access to one method of overcoming mind-affecting immunity, from the following list. Each time they would gain a bold focus, they may instead opt to take an additional method from this list.

Echoes of Life: Just as negative energy can create the facsimile of a living thing, the mesmerist can mold it to be as susceptible as a living thing. Doing so is a full-round action. Against mindless undead, this allows the mesmerist (and only the mesmerist) to ignore the creature’s immunities to mind-affecting spells and abilities. An intelligent undead becomes subject to all mind-affecting spells and abilities. In both cases, the undead is treated as if it has the same creature type it had while alive.
Mind Emulation: Intelligent constructs and robots are complex machines with the capacity to harbor a rich (and exploitable) internal experience. They were simply never granted the necessary functions. As a full-round action, the mesmerist can imbue one with these functions. The rigid programming of the target naturally resists the intrusion, granting it a Will saving throw to resist the effect. The save DC is 10 + 1/2 the mesmerist’s level + the mesmerist’s Charisma modifier. On a failure, the target becomes subject to all mind-affecting spells and abilities as if it was a humanoid.
Mortalize Native: As a move action, by drawing the perspective of a native outsider to see the world through the lens of mortals, the mesmerist causes it to become subject to all mind-affecting spells and abilities as if it was a humanoid.
Quiet the Inner Beast: As a move action, the mesmerist distances a monstrous humanoid from the wild aspects of its mind. It becomes subject to all mind-affecting spells and abilities as if it was a humanoid.
Suspend Protection: As a standard action, the mesmerist’s will touches the surface of a mind, feels out its weak points, and stretches them open to enter. This temporarily allows the mesmerist (and only the mesmerist) to ignore immunities not dependent on the target’s creature type to any mind-affecting effects, as well as its resistance bonuses on Will saving throws for 1 round. To hold the mind open to influence in subsequent rounds, the mesmerist must concentrate as a move action.
Taking Root: Influencing the mind of an intelligent plant requires a mesmerist to worm their influence through its passive defenses in a laborious process that takes 1 round. Completion allows the mesmerist (and only the mesmerist) to ignore the creature’s immunities to mind-affecting spells and abilities.
Trigger Emergence: As a standard action, the mesmerist can trick the base instincts and simple programming of a mindless construct, ooze, plant, robot or vermin to approximate a mind for a short while. This allows the mesmerist (and only the mesmerist) to ignore the creature’s immunities to mind-affecting spells and abilities. Even after the mesmerist shifts their hypnotic focus elsewhere, mind-affecting spells and abilities the target already suffered continue to function as if the target wasn’t immune.
Mesmerist Tricks (Su)

A mesmerist can create hypnotic bonds with his allies. This is identical to the classic mesmerist class feature.

Towering Ego (Su)

At 2nd level, the legendary mesmerist gains towering ego, identical to the classic mesmerist class feature.

Metamagic Feat

At certain levels, the legendary mesmerist may choose a bonus feat without fulfilling its prerequisites. It 4th level, they can choose either Heighten Spell or Extend Spell. At 8th level, they may also choose Echoing Spell or Studied Spell.

Manifold Tricks (Su)

At 5th level, a mesmerist gains manifold tricks, identical to the classic mesmerist class feature.

Rental Potency (Ex)

At 5th level, a legendary mesmerist gains mental potency, identical to the classic mesmerist class feature.

Focus Breach (Su)

At 10th level, spells the legendary mesmerist perfected the bypass of all mental barriers. When casting a focus spell on a target of their hypnotic focus using a higher spell slot than its original level (either by choice or as part of applying a metamagic effect), the mesmerist can also use an ability of their choice from the impose psyche class feature as part of the same action, whether or not they have that ability. When used in this way, impose psyche takes effect before the spell.

Masterful Tricks (Su)

At 12th level, a mesmerist gains access to masterful tricks. This is identical to the classic mesmerist class feature.

Dominion (Su)

At 20th level, the legendary mesmerist’s hypnotic focus extends to medium range (100 feet + 10 feet per level). Within its range, they are automatically aware of any creature without needing to succeed on a Perception check, whether or not these creatures have an Intelligence score, and any mind-affecting effects. This otherwise functions as blindsense.

Hypnotic Foci
Curse

“Just think of all the choices you have to serve me.”

This focus is a bane upon the free will of others, and mesmerists who have it can be blatantly ominous. It is a curse effect, and whenever it is used, creatures aware of both the mesmerist and at least one of their targets reflexively roll a Sense Motive check with a DC equal to 15 + mesmerist’s level. Any creature who succeeds realizes the mesmerist used a harmful effect and is aware whenever it is the target of the focus as long as it is also aware of the mesmerist, for the next 24 hours.

Target: Single

Double: The penalty doubles when the target of the focus has been under the same harmful effect for at least 24 hours.

Bonus Feat: Bold Enforcer*

Bonus Spell: hibernate

Diminish Will: The target may take actions that use its base attack bonus, harmful spells and harmful abilities only at the mesmerist’s direction. At 8th level, this limitation extends to ability checks. At 16th level, it extends to movement, mundane or magical. While it cannot take these actions independently, it isn’t obligated to follow the mesmerist’s orders, but suffers the penalties of enforcement until it does. Enforcement: The target takes a penalty to an ability score of the mesmerist’s choice. The choice is made each time the ability is used. A target may suffer different penalties to multiple ability scores at a time from different uses of diminish.

External

“Out of sight, in your mind.”

For the mesmerist to stretch and contort minds outside the limits of physical possibility, their limited physical form mustn’t be perceived. To apply focus to a target, it must not know the location of the mesmerist down to the mesmerist’s space. Being disguised as something else is not sufficient – the mesmerist mustn’t be directly noticed for the focus to work. More vague notions of the mesmerist’s location(such as ‘in the other room’, ‘that way’, or ‘behind this illusory wall’) do not impede their focus.

Target: Multiple

Double: The penalty is doubled whenever the target does not know the mesmerist exists.

Bonus Feat: Skill Focus (Stealth)

Bonus Spell: vanish

Censor: Will: Any target the mesmerist maintains their focus on is subtly influenced to not notice them, such as by turning in the wrong direction at just the right time, glancing over their hiding place, or keeping them in its blind spot. It automatically fails its Perception checks opposing the mesmerist’s Stealth checks. Enforcement: Each target feels as though perceiving the mesmerist’s existence was against the natural order. It becomes sickened whenever it does. Whenever it loses track of the mesmerist’s location, it must attempt another saving throw against censor.

Fear

“Horror… Horror has a face.”

The mesmerist uses fear as the vehicle of his mental control. The target of the hypnotic focus is automatically affected if it’s under a fear effect. If the creature is not currently affected by a fear effect, the mesmerist must demoralize it as a move action. This demoralize attempt enables the use of the hypnotic focus on the target for 1 round whether or not it’s successful, even if the target is immune to fear.

Target: Multiple

Double: The penalty doubles against a creature that is frightened, panicked, or cowering.

Bonus Feat: Skill Focus (Intimidate)

Bonus Spell: hidden diplomacy

Subsuming Terror

Will: Targets act as though their attitude towards the mesmerist was friendly. After 1 round spent not interacting with the mesmerist, targets avoid any interactions with the mesmerist to the best of their ability, and otherwise act normally until they interact with the mesmerist again. This otherwise functions as being coerced by an Intimidate check.

Effect Targets are shaken whenever in combat against the mesmerist. Each time a target rests long enough to recover ability damage, roll one die after that damage is recovered. The number of faces on the die equals the penalty. The target suffers Wisdom damage equal to the result. This wisdom damage is independent of Will Enforcement. If a target’s Wisdom score would be reduced to 0 in this way, it remains at 1, but the target bows to the mesmerist’s will as if it failed its saving throw.

“Show of hands: Who’s with me?…Why, it’s everybody!”

The mesmerist projects their hypnotic focus by presenting their palm, holding their temples, or making strange, serpentine motions with their fingers, pulling others through puppet strings and molding them like clay. Their focus requires a free hand for as long as it’s maintained. Using a hand in this way is considered a somatic component, and its use is affected by arcane spell failure.

Target: Single

Double: The mesmerist can double the penalty by using all their hands to project their focus.

Bonus Feat: Skill Focus (Sleight of Hand)

Bonus Spell: fumbletongue

Puppeteer

Will: While it is also the target of your hypnotic focus, you can usurp the connection between the target’s mind and body to control it like a marionette. It can be made to take simple actions such as dropping prone, standing up or carrying items, acting on your initiative instead of its own. Its motions are robotic, twitching, jerking or otherwise unnatural. It can be made to move, though its speed is reduced by 5. Forcing it to take actions harmful to it grants it an additional saving throw against the effect. It cannot be forced to take any action that requires a roll or check. The mesmerist may prevent it from communicating in ways other than telepathy, but cannot force it to communicate anything other than gibberish.

Enforcement: The target loses fine control of its appendages. Its speed is reduced by 5. It suffers a penalty to Dexterity-based skill checks, as well as Craft, Perform and Artistry checks. If it uses its Dexterity modifier for its attacks or damage, those also suffer a penalty. Its spells with somatic components suffer a 10% spell failure chance.

Alternate Rules
Alternate Capstones

If alternate capstones are used, the legendary mesmerist may take the rule minds ability of the classic mesmerist as their capstone.

Retraining

When using the retraining rules, the legendary mesmerist is considered to have retraining synergy with the arcanist, bard, bloodrager, medium, skald, sorcerer, spiritualist and psychic classes, as well as vice versa. When retraining class features, the legendary mesmerist may retrain one bold focus or mesmerist trick at a time. Retraining hypnotic focus takes at least 15 days, plus 2 days per spell level to replace focus spells known that are not on your resulting spell list.

For The Classic Mesmerist

The classic mesmerist is a capable class, limited only in its scope and flavor. The legendary mesmerist is not meant to be a replacement. Instead, the two are counterparts of each other that can coexist in the same campaign, with the former a powerful spellcaster, and the latter a versatile generalist. There are no multiclass mesmerist/legendary mesmerists – a character may only take one or the other. The classic mesmerist can use some character options of the legendary mesmerist as follows:

Alternate Capstones

If alternate capstones are used, the classic mesmerist may take the dominion ability of the legendary mesmerist as their capstone.

Bold Foci

A classic mesmerist may take bold foci as bold stares.

Impose Psyche

At the GM’s discretion, the classic mesmerist may take abilities from impose psyche in place of bold stares, losing access to the psychic inception bold stare.

Spellcasting

All new spells of 6th level or lower in this book are also available to the classic mesmerist. Optionally, core spells added to the legendary mesmerist spell list at those spell levels may also be added to the classic mesmerist spell list at the GM’s discretion.

Retraining

When using the retraining rules, the classic mesmerist has the same retraining synergies as the legendary mesmerist. They also have synergy with each other. When retraining class features, the classic mesmerist may retrain one mesmerist trick or bold stare at a time. Exchanging hypnotic stare for a hypnotic focus or vice versa works the same way as gaining or abandoning an archetype. Both take the same amount of time as it does for the mesmerist to change foci, except for the stare focus, which takes 10 days at the minimum instead of 15. The classic mesmerist changing from one focus to another requires two retraining sessions: one to abandon the current one, and then one to gain the new one.

Hypnotic Foci

A classic mesmerist treats hypnotic foci as archetypes. Raining a hypnotic focus replaces consummate liar, painful stare, and glib lie. Excepting the stare focus, it also alters hypnotic stare.

Focused Caster

A classic mesmerist with a hypnotic focus adds its respective focus spells of 6th level and lower not already on the mesmerist spell list to their spell list. They begin play with the bonus feat, bonus spell, and will enforcement specific to the focus. However, at 1st level and whenever they gain access to a new spell level, one of the spells they learn at that level must be a focus spell.

This alters the mesmerist’s spellcasting. In addition to the foci listed above, these foci are intended for the classic mesmerist. The legendary mesmerist may also take these foci. If a spell gained from these foci is not on the mesmerist spell list, the legendary mesmerist adds it at the highest spell level it appears on any spell list.

Sybarite

None other as bright. The mesmerist channels their focus through well-made or personal items. To use their focus, the mesmerist must have access to an item they created personally, or one worth at least one-tenth of their recommended wealth by level, worn on their person, held, or touched. If such an item is worn by another creature who is not the mesmerist’s ally, the mesmerist may achieve focus for 1 round by succeeding on a melee touch attack against it.

Target: Multiple

Double: The penalty doubles while the items worn, held and touched by the mesmerist have a market price in excess of their recommended wealth by level when put together.

Bonus Feat: Skill Focus (Appraise)

Bonus Spell: true appraisal

Remade Whole Cloth

Will: Targets perceive the mesmerist’s sense of style as world-leading, if not outright objective. In addition to the effects of enforcement, they will not resist the mesmerist’s harmless focus spells, and will not perceive any focus spell the mesmerist casts, nor this ability, to be a hostile action, whether targeted at them or others. Remade whole cloth does not prevent targets from trying to undo the effects of these spells, but they will not make an attempt until the spells become detrimental to their targets in some way.

Enforcement: Targets suffer a penalty to saving throws against sybarite focus spells. This stacks with the penalty of hypnotic foci, up to -4.
